lens: Prospective applicant — long or difficult content; simulated user lens
reason: The reviewed public proposition is clear: student-led, pro-bono consulting, with an obvious student route and an every-major eligibility statement. Supplied home captures show coherent Precision Instrument typography, restrained structure and readable mobile actions. I traced Home → Join → Apply → recovery/review/submission → applicant next action through actual source and inspected synthetic journey tests and their passing log. Preparation guidance, response word counts, explicit draft-versus-submit copy, consent reset and schedule-outage messaging support this task. The materials and review steps accurately disclose access to original identifying resumes. However, recovering substantial writing still imposes an avoidable comparison/retention burden, and supplied checks use short responses rather than difficult content. No private-screen capture or hosted integration demonstrates that an applicant can complete this journey successfully. This is independent AI source/evidence review, not observed student success or an unqualified world-class endorsement.

findings.evidence: The revision-conflict screen renders every RECOVERY_FIELDS entry and every question, including identical values, followed by the two whole-copy actions. RecoveryComparison prints both complete texts without identifying changes. The instruction at line 622 requires copying wanted text before choosing; resolveConflict replaces the entire answers object and clears browser recovery when selecting the saved copy. In contrast, the earlier browser-recovery screen filters unchanged fields (595-602). The conflict fixture in tests/e2e/application-reliability.spec.ts:231-260 changes only a name; the browser-recovery fixture at 155-201 uses single-sentence answers.
findings.userImpact: When useful revisions exist in different essays across devices, a student must find differences among duplicated content and manually preserve text outside the paused form before a destructive whole-copy choice. Long mobile comparisons amplify that burden. This is a source-supported interaction limitation, not an observed data-loss incident.
findings.suggestedFix: Show changed fields first, offer per-response selection into a reviewable combined draft, and preserve both originals until the combined draft is acknowledged. Add a focused mobile fixture with long responses changed in different fields and verify retention through recovery.
